When you format text, the system automatically converts it into standard HTML tags for the website. Here is what each tool creates behind the scenes: • Text Formatting • Bold (B): Wraps text in tags to make it bold. • Italic (I): Wraps text in tags for emphasis/italics. • H2, H3, H4: Creates heading tags

or container tags at the cursor position.

•  Alignment

•  Align center: Applies text-align: center via inline styles or CSS classes to the block.

•  Justify: Applies text-align: justify to evenly space text across the line.

•  Lists

•  Numbered list: Creates an ordered list using <ol> and <li> tags.

•  Bulleted list: Creates an unordered list using <ul> and <li> tags.

I N S E RT  L I N K

•  Insert External Link

•  Link to a page outside your website. Select the External link tab, paste the destination URL (required), enter the Link
   text, and click Insert Link. A preview of the link is shown before insertion. This creates a standard HTML <a> tag
   pointing to an external address.

•  Insert Internal Link

•  Link to another page within your own website. Select the Internal link tab, type keywords in Search pages to find the
   target article, enter the Link text, select the desired page from the results, and click Insert Link. This creates an HTML
  <a> tag using your site's internal URL.

I N S E RT   I M A G E  F RO M R I C H - T E X T E D I T O R

•  Click the Image button in the content editor toolbar to open the image selection modal. From here,
  you can select an existing image from the media library or upload a new one.
•  Choose an Image – Search
• On the Search tab, browse the media library. Use the search bar to find images by title, then click on
  any thumbnail to select it. Use the pagination controls at the bottom to navigate through the library.
•  Choose an Image – Upload
•  Switch to the Upload tab to add a new image. Click Choose File to select an image from your device
  (supported formats: AVIF, GIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, WEBP; maximum 1.0 MB). Enter a Title (required),
  and optionally add a Caption, Tags, and Attribute. Click Upload to save the image to the library and
  proceed.
• Add Image Caption & Alignment
•  After selecting or uploading an image, the Add Image Caption modal opens. A preview of the image
  appears at the top.
•  Caption: Enter or edit the image caption text.
•  Alignment: Select how the image will display in the article, such as Full width, Left, or Right.
•  Click Insert Image to place the image into the article with the applied caption and alignment settings.

•  Click the Table option from the content editor's insert menu to add a data table to your article. In the modal,
   enter the number of Rows and Columns you need (default is 2x2), then click Add to insert the table or Cancel to
   close without adding.

• Once inserted, the table appears directly inside the content editor as an editable grid. Click on any cell to start
   typing or pasting content. The table is rendered within the article body using standard HTML table markup,
   allowing you to present structured data clearly.

I N S E RT G A L L E RY

•  Click the Gallery button in the content editor toolbar to open the image selection modal and create an image
   gallery.
•  Select Multiple Images – Search
• On the Search tab, browse the media library. Use the search bar to find images by title. Click on multiple images to
   select them; a checkmark appears on each selected item. The bottom of the modal shows how many images are
   selected (for example, "3 selected"). Use pagination to browse more images. Once you have selected all desired
   images, click Insert Gallery to add them to the article.
•  Upload New Images – Upload
•  Switch to the Upload tab to add new images directly to the gallery. Click Choose File to select an image from your
   device (supported formats: AVIF, GIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, WEBP; maximum 1.0 MB). Enter a Title (required), and
   optionally add a Caption, Tags, and Attribute. Click Upload to save the image. You can upload multiple images this
  way before inserting the gallery.
•  Gallery in the Content Editor
•  After insertion, a gallery block labeled Gallery 1 appears in the article. Each image in the gallery displays with:
• An SL No field to set the serial or sort order.
• A Caption field to add a description for each image.
• A red X button on each image to remove it individually.
•  Use the Add more image button to open the modal again and add additional photos to the existing gallery. Use the
   blue up/down arrows to move the entire gallery block within the content, or click the red X at the top-right to
   delete the whole gallery.

I N S E RT Y O U T U B E V I D E O

•  Click the YouTube video option from the content editor's insert menu to embed a YouTube video. In the modal, paste the
  YouTube URL into the field (supports both youtube.com and youtu.be links). A live Preview of the video appears
   automatically below the URL field so you can confirm the correct video before inserting it. Click Insert Video to embed it
   into the article, or Cancel to close without adding.

• Once inserted, the video appears as an embedded player directly inside the content editor with a play button overlay. Use the
   top-right toolbar on the video block to expand the view, move the video up or down within the content, or remove it.

I N S E RT  S O C I A L E M B E D

•  Click the Social Embed option from the content editor's insert menu to add external content. In the modal, paste the
   platform's embed code (such as an <iframe>) into the Embed code field. The system automatically detects the source
   platform (for example, "iframe from youtube.com"). Click Insert to place the embed into your article.

• Once inserted, a live preview of the embedded content appears directly in the content editor. Use the arrow buttons on
   the block to move it up or down within the article, or click the red delete button to remove it.

•  Choose a Document – Upload

•  Switch to the Upload tab to add a new PDF. Enter a Title (required), click Choose File to select a PDF from

I N S E RT A L S O R E A D

•  Click the AlsoRead button in the content editor toolbar to recommend a related story within your article. A
  modal titled Choose Add story will open, displaying a searchable list of all published (LIVE) articles. Use the
   search bar to find a specific story, then click on the desired title to select it.

I N S E RT E D P D F P RE V I E W

•  Once inserted, an ALSO READ block appears inside the content editor showing the linked story title. You
   can reposition the block using the up and down arrows, or remove it by clicking the red delete button.

I N S E RT D I V I D E R L I N E


 Click the Divider line option from the content editor's insert menu to add a horizontal separating line
 between sections of your article. Once inserted, a block labeled "Divider line" appears in the editor with a
  visual horizontal rule. On the published page, this renders as an HTML <hr> tag to create a clear content
 break.

C O N T E N T B L O C K B U T T O N S
•  Below the main editor, these buttons let you quickly add special content blocks and access writing tools:

•  Richtext: Opens an additional rich-text editor block to create a new content section within the article.

•  AlsoRead: Inserts a related story recommendation block linking to another article.

•  Embed: Adds a block for external content such as social media posts or iframe embeds.

•  Gallery: Inserts an image gallery block to display multiple photos.

•  Image: Adds a single image block into the article body.

•  Fullscreen: Expands the editor to full-screen mode for distraction-free writing.

•  Generate Headline: Automatically suggests or generates a headline based on the article content.

•  Proof Read: Runs a proofreading check to review the article for errors or improvements.

•  Content Statistics

• The bar above the buttons shows live stats comparing content up to the cursor versus the full article: Words,
   Paragraphs, Characters, and Characters without spaces.

A D D  S U M M A RY

•  Toggle the Enable Summary switch to activate the article summary feature. When enabled, an Add Summary modal opens where
  you can write a brief overview of the article manually, or click Generate with AI to create one automatically from the news
   content. The summary is limited to 1000 characters, with a live counter showing your current length. Click Add to save the
  summary, or Cancel to close without saving.

• Once added, the summary appears as a dedicated block within the article. You can click the Edit button next to the toggle at
  any time to modify the summary content.

C A T E G O RY ,  S U B C A T E G O RY &  P I N T O C A T E G O RY  P A G E

In the Add News form, you can assign a story to multiple categories and subcategories. Select the desired items from
the dropdowns for each field. One category and one subcategory can be marked as Primary to set the main
classification.

The Pin in category page section shows toggles for each selected category. Turn a toggle on to pin the story to the
top of that category's public page as the lead story. The pinned item remains fixed in the lead position until you
change or remove it.

T A G S

• Assign one or more tags to the article using the multi-select dropdown. Selected tags
  appear as chips at the top of the field. Click the X on any chip to remove a tag. Use the
  Search field to quickly find and select tags from the existing list.

R E F E R E N C E N E W S
• Link up to 3 related news articles to the current story using the multi-select dropdown.
  Selected articles appear as chips at the top of the field; click the X to remove any selection.
  Use the Search field to quickly find articles from the list. A maximum of 3 reference news
  items can be selected.

F E A T U RE D  I T E M S

 •  Select a featured section where the story will be prominently displayed, such as Lead Section, Second Lead, LiveFeatured, or
   FeaturedVideo.

 •  After selecting a section, choose a Position (0 to 9) to set the story's placement order within that section. The News Sorting

S C H E D U L E P U B L I S H I N G

•  Click the Schedule button at the bottom of the Add News form to set a future publication date and time. In the modal,
   click the Publish date & time field and select the desired date and time from the picker (required).

• Once a date and time are selected, a confirmation box appears showing the exact scheduled time (for example, "Monday,
  26 October 2026 at 12:07") and a countdown (for example, "Publishes in 21 hours, 18 minutes"). Review the details, then
   click Schedule Publish to confirm. The article will be published automatically at the selected moment. Click Cancel to
   close the modal without scheduling.

A C T I O N B U T T O N S

•  At the bottom of the Add News form, the action bar lets you finalize the article:

•  Mobile Preview: Preview how the article will look on a mobile device.

•  Desktop Preview: Preview how the article will appear on a desktop screen.

•  Publish: Make the article live on the website immediately.

•  Save as Draft: Save the article without publishing so you can edit it later.

•  Schedule: Set a future date and time for the article to be published automatically.

•  Article Preview

•  Click the Mobile or Desktop preview button to open a live preview of the article before publishing. The preview
  shows exactly how the headline, content, and layout will appear to readers on the public website. Toggle between

•  Story Details

•  Headline: Enter the main headline for the photo news story (required).

•  Sub Heading: Add an optional subheading.

•  Alternative Headline: Provide an alternate headline if needed.

•  Highlight: Mark the story as a highlight if applicable.

•  Photo Content & Gallery

•  Photo Content: Write the main narrative or description using the rich-text editor. Use the toolbar to format text, add
   headings, lists, links, and other media.

•  Photo Blocks: Build your photo story by uploading images one by one. Each block (for example, Photo 1) includes a
  Choose Image button, a Caption field to describe the image, and arrow/trash buttons to reorder or remove that photo.
  Click the green + Add More button to add additional photo blocks and create a multi-image gallery story.

•  Content & Excerpt

•  Content: Use this additional rich-text area to add supplementary descriptions or text content for the story.

•  Excerpt: Write a short summary to display on the homepage (maximum 300 words)

•  Uploaded By: Enter the name or credit of the person who uploaded the content.

Author & Classification (Right Panel)
•Author: Select the author(s), up to 3 (required).
•Author Location: Enter the author's location if applicable.
•Initial: Select an initial identifier from the dropdown.
•Tags: Assign relevant tags to the story.
•Display Title: Enter a short title for display purposes (maximum 100 characters).
•Pin in category page: Toggle on to pin this story to the top of its category page. The latest pinned story appears at the top.

Media & SEO
•News Image: Upload the main featured image for the photo news story (required).
•Meta Title: Enter the SEO page title (maximum 255 characters).
•Meta Description: Write the descriptive text shown underneath the headline in search engine results.
•Meta Keyword: Add keywords for search engine optimization (maximum 500 characters).

Publishing Options (Bottom Bar)
•Mobile Preview: Preview how the photo story will appear on mobile devices.
•Desktop Preview: Preview how it will appear on desktop screens.
•Publish: Make the photo news story live on the website immediately.

•  Insert Menu (+ Insert)

•  Click the + Insert dropdown to add special content blocks within the photo story:

•  Image: Insert a single image into the content area.

•  Table: Add a data table by specifying rows and columns.

•  YouTube video: Embed a YouTube video by pasting the video URL.

•  Divider line: Insert a horizontal line (<hr>) to separate content sections.

•  Insert Link

•  Click the link icon in the toolbar to create hyperlinks. Choose between:

•  Internal link: Search and link to another page within your website.

•  External link: Paste an external URL and set the link text.

•  Click Insert Link to add the hyperlink to the content.

•  More Options (Three Dots)

•  Click the three-dots menu for additional formatting tools:

•  Align center: Center-align the current text block.

•   Justify: Evenly space text across the line width.

•  Find & replace: Search for specific text and replace it throughout the content.

•  Unpin toolbar: Allow the toolbar to scroll with the page instead of remaining fixed at the top.

•  Standard Formatting

•  Use the toolbar buttons for everyday text styling:

•  H2, H3, H4: Apply heading levels to structure the content.

• B (Bold): Make text bold using <strong>.
•   I (Italic): Italicize text using <em>.

•  Big fact: Highlight key facts or statistics in a styled block.

•  Numbered list / Bulleted list: Create ordered (<ol>) or unordered (<ul>) lists.

A D D V I D E O N E W S  F O R M

•  USE THIS FORM TO CREATE AND PUBLISH A VIDEO-BASED NEWS STORY
   Story Details

•  Headline: Enter the main headline for the video news story (required).

•  Sub Heading: Add an optional subheading.

•  Content: Write the article body or video description using the rich-text editor. Use the toolbar to format text, add
   headings, lists, links, and insert media.

•  Excerpt: Write a short summary to display on the homepage (maximum 300 words).

•  Uploaded By: Enter the name or credit of the person who uploaded the content.

•  Alternative Title: Provide an alternate title if needed.

•  Author & Classification (Right Panel)

•  Author: Select the author(s), up to 3 (required).

•  Author Location: Enter the author's location if applicable.

•  Initial: Select an initial identifier from the dropdown.

•  This page displays a centralized list of all content created in the CMS, including standard news articles, video stories,
  photo stories, web stories, and live news updates.

•  Top Controls

• Add Story: Click the dropdown button to quickly create a new story. Choose from the available story types to jump
   directly to the relevant creation form.

•  Search stories: Use the search bar to find specific stories by typing keywords from the title or content.

•  Drafts: Click the Drafts button to filter and view only unpublished stories saved as drafts.

•  Filters / View Options: Use the filter and layout icons to refine the list by criteria such as story type, status, or author,
  and switch between list or grid views.

•  Pagination: The top of the list shows the current range (for example, "Showing 1–25 of 171"). Use the Per page
  dropdown to change how many stories display at once (for example, 25, 50, or 100).

•  Story List Table

•  Each row in the table represents one story with the following columns:

•  Checkbox: Select one or multiple stories to perform bulk actions.

•  Title: The headline of the story. Click the title to open the story in Edit mode.

•  View: Click the View link (external link icon) to open and see how the story appears on the live public
   website.

•  Updated: Shows when the story was last modified (for example, "23 hr ago" or "6 days ago").

•  Created By: Displays the name of the user who originally created the story.

•  Updated By: Displays the name of the user who last edited the story.

•  Type: Indicates the story format, such as "Add story" (standard news), "Video story", "Photo story", or "Web
   story".

•  Status: Shows the current publication state. LIVE means the story is published and visible on the website.
  DRAFT means the story is unpublished and only visible in the admin panel.
• Row Actions

•  Three-dot menu: Click the menu icon on any row to access additional options:
   History: View the edit history and activity log for that story.
   Preview: Open the story in the editor (edit page) to review or modify it before publishing.

•  Bulk Actions

•  Select one or more stories using the checkboxes on the left. When items are selected, a floating action bar
   appears at the bottom showing how many are selected (for example, "2 selected"). From this bar you can:

•  Publish: Publish all selected draft stories at once, making them live.

•  Unpublish: Unpublish all selected live stories. Unpublished stories are moved to the Drafts list and are no
   longer visible on the public site.

•  Cancel: Clear the current selection without performing any action.

•  Status Indicators

•  Stories marked LIVE are actively displayed on the website.

•  Stories marked DRAFT are saved but not yet published. Any story you unpublish will automatically return
   to the Drafts list.

•  Access the history of any story by clicking the three-dot menu on the story list and selecting History. This
  opens a timeline showing every major action taken on that article.

  summary of which fields were modified (for example, "Changed: Excerpt, LocationAuthor, LastPublishedAt,

•  Each history entry includes a view detail link to see the full specifics of that change.

F U L L H I S T O RY P A G E

•  Clicking the story title hyperlink from the modal (or navigating directly) opens the dedicated Story History page.
  This page provides the same chronological timeline in a full-screen layout, displaying the story title, story type
   (for example, "News"), story ID, and a complete log of all creation and edit events with timestamps and changed
   field details. Use the back arrow to return to the stories list.

A U D I T D E T A I L  P A G E

•  Click view detail from any entry in the Story History timeline(bottom of every log) to open the full audit log
   for that specific change. This page provides a complete breakdown of exactly what was modified in a single

•  Audit Header

•  Audit ID: Displays the unique audit number (for example, "Audit Detail #576").

•  Action & Status: Shows the action type (for example, "update") and whether it was successful.

•  Story Reference: Indicates which story was affected (for example, "on news #173") along with the story
   headline.

•  User & Timestamp: Displays the user who made the change (for example, "Rafi Rahman"), the exact date and
   time, IP address, and how long the action took to process.

•  Publication State: Badges show whether the story was published before the change ("Was Published") and after
   the change ("Is Now Published").

•  Field Changes Table

• The main section lists every field that was modified in this edit. The table has three columns:

•  Field: The name of the modified field (for example, Excerpt, Last Published At, Author Location, Locked,
  Locked At, Locked By).

•  Old Value: The previous value before the edit. If a field was empty or unchanged, this may be blank.

• New Value: The updated value after the edit.

• The Last Published At timestamp was updated from "25/10/2026 05:13:45" to "26/10/2026 06:26:31".

• The Author Location was changed to "ঢাকা".

• The Locked status changed from "True" to "False".

• The Locked At and Locked By fields were cleared.

•  View Modes

•  At the top-right of the changes table, three tabs let you switch how the data is displayed:

•  Plain Text: Shows values in simple readable text.

•  Rich P review: Renders formatted or styled content where applicable.

•  Raw: Displays the raw data values as stored in the system.

V I E W  S T O RY O N P U B L I C  S I T E

•  From the All Stories list, click the View button (external link icon) next to any story to open and review how it
   appears on the live public website. This opens the article in a new browser tab using the actual front -end URL,
  showing exactly what readers will see.

•  Click the filter icon(after Draft button) on the All Stories page to open the filter panel. You can filter the story
    list by multiple criteria to quickly find specific content. Select your desired filters, then click Apply Filters to
  update the list, or Reset to clear all selections.

D A T E  F I L T E R

•  Narrow down stories by publication or creation date. Enter a From and To date using the date picker, or use
   the Quick Select shortcuts to instantly choose Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, or This month.
  Click Done to confirm your date selection.

•  Filter by the format of the content. Select one or more types from the list:

• Add story (standard news)

•  Live story

•  Photo story

•  Video story

• Web story

•  Shorts / Reels

•  Quote story

F I L T E R B Y C A T E G O RY &  S U B C A T E G O RY

•  Filter stories by their assigned Category or SubCategory. Use the search box at the top of each list to quickly find a
   category, then check the boxes to select one or more. SubCategory options can be filtered after selecting a parent
   category.

F I L T E R B Y O W N E R N A M E

•  Filter stories by the user who created them. Use the search box to find a specific author or editor, then
  check the names you want to include in the filtered results.

•  After making selections in any filter section, click Done to confirm that section, then click Apply Filters on
   the main panel to refresh the story list.

P A G I N A T I O N C O N T RO L S

•  Use the Per page dropdown to change how many stories display on a single page. Choose from 25, 50, 100, 150, 200,
   or 300 items per page. The list will refresh automatically to show the selected number of stories.

• The Showing indicator above the table updates to reflect the current view, for example "Showing 1–100 of 171",

   conflicting edits by multiple users at the same time. Hover over the lock icon to see the name of the user
  who has locked the story.

•   If another user needs to edit the same story, they can unlock it using the three -dot menu next to the story
  row and selecting Unlock, provided they have the necessary unlock permission. Once unlocked, the story

C O L L E C T I O N S

•  Collections are grouped content sections that control how stories appear together on the website frontend. The
   Collections List page displays all available content groups (for example, LeadSection, SecondLead, VideoSection,
   EditorsPick) and lets you manage their structure, content source, and display order.

•  Collections List

• The main list shows all collection groups with the following details:

•  Group Order: Numbered sequence showing the display order on the page.

•  Collection Name: The identifier for the section (for example, LeadSection, EightStoriesLeftBig).

•  Mode: Shows whether the collection is AUTO (automatically populated), MANUAL (curated by editors), or
  STATIC (pulled from a custom data source).

•  Source Info: Displays the assigned category, tag, or featured item feeding the collection.

•  Slots: Shows how many content slots exist within the group (for example, "3 slots").

•  Actions:
   •+ Slot: Add a new content slot to the collection.
   •Expand arrow: Click to expand the collection and view or manage its individual slots.
   •Edit: Modify the collection settings.
   •Delete: Remove the entire collection group.

R E O R D E R C O L L E C T I O N S


•  Drag and drop collection groups using the handle icons to rearrange their display order. Once you have
  arranged the sections in the desired sequence, click the Save Order button at the top right to apply the
   changes. The saved order determines exactly how these sections appear on the public website.

E X P A N D  S L O T S    ( A R R O W  B U T T O N )


   Click the arrow next to any collection to expand it and reveal its internal slots. Each slot represents a specific
   content position or sub-section within that collection. The expanded view shows the slot number, story type
  (Manual/Automatic/Static), and the source name. Each slot can be edited or deleted individually from this view.

A D D N E W  S L O T T O A C O L L E C T I O N

•  Click the + Slot button on any collection row to add a new content slot. The form inherits the Template Name
  from the parent group (for example, "LeadSection") and lets you choose the Slot Number (for example, "Slot 4").

•  Select a Story Type:

•  Automatic: Pulls stories automatically from a chosen source.

•  Manual: Links to a featured item.

•  Static: Uses a data source identifier.

•  For Automatic slots, choose the News Source by Category / Subcategory or Tag. In the example, Slot 4 was added to
   the LeadSection collection using Automatic mode with the সারা দেশ (National) category as the source. Once saved,
   the new slot appears in the expanded collection list and feeds content into that section on the public site.

•  Author List

•  This page displays all authors in the CMS. The list shows each author's profile image, name, author type (Normal, Special,

•  Search & Filter

   the author's details and all news stories written by them.

• Row Actions

•  Edit (pencil): Modify the author's profile information.

•  Special toggle (star): Switch the author between Normal and Special status.

•  Delete (trash): Remove the author from the system.

•  Edit the Meta Title, Meta Description (maximum 500 characters), and Meta Keywords to optimize the author's

•  This page lists all content categories in the CMS. The table displays each category's Name, Slug, and Meta Title status.
  Use the Search field to find categories by name or slug. Click + Add Category to create a new category, or use the
   Edit (pencil) and Delete (trash) icons on each row to manage existing ones.

C R E A T E C A T E G O RY

Use this form to add a new category.
•Name: Enter the category name (required).
•Slug: The URL-friendly identifier, auto-generated from the name. Click the Lock icon to edit it manually.
•Watermark Image: Upload a watermark image for this category. Must be exactly 1200 x 100 px, JPG/JPEG only,
maximum 2 MB.
A Live Preview on the right shows how the category label will appear.

• SEO & Meta

•  Optimize the category page for search engines:

•  Meta Title: The page title shown in browser tabs and search results.

•  Meta Description: A brief description for search engine results.

•  Meta Keywords: Relevant keywords separated by commas.

•  Click Create Category to save, or Cancel to discard.

E D I T C A T E G O RY

• Click the edit (pencil) icon on any category row to open the Edit Category form. Update the
  Name, Slug, and Watermark Image (JPG/JPEG, exactly 1200 x 100 px, max 2 MB). The slug
  can be manually edited by clicking the Edit button, and the system confirms availability. The
  Live Preview on the right shows the updated category label.

•  In the SEO & Meta section, update the Meta Title, Meta Description, and Meta Keywords to optimize the
   category page for search engines.

•  Click Save Changes to apply updates, or Cancel to discard them.

S U B - C A T E G O R I E S

• The Subcategories page lists all subcategories under their parent categories. The table shows each subcategory's
  Name, Parent Category, Slug, and Meta Title status. Use the Search field to find subcategories by name or slug, and
   filter by parent category using the All Categories dropdown. Click + Add Subcategory to create a new one.

C R E A T E  S U B C A T E G O RY

•  In the creation form, select a Parent Category (required), then enter the subcategory Name and Slug. The slug
   auto-generates from the name; click the Lock icon to edit it manually. The Live Preview panel shows how the
  subcategory label will appear.

•  In the SEO & Meta section, add a Meta Title, Meta Description, and Meta Keywords to optimize the
  subcategory page for search engines. Click Create Subcategory to save, or Cancel to discard.

E D I T  S U B C A T E G O RY

•  Click the edit option on any subcategory row to open the edit form with all fields pre -filled. Update the Parent
   Category, Name, or Slug as needed. The slug can be manually edited and the system will confirm availability.
  Adjust the SEO & Meta fields if required. The Live Preview updates in real time. Click Save Changes to apply
   updates, or Cancel to discard them.

M E N U M A N A G E M E N T

•  This section controls the navigation menus displayed on the public website.

• Menu List

• The main page lists all navigation menus (for example, "Menu" and "Footer Menu 2"). Each menu shows its item
  count and action buttons to Manage, Edit, or Delete. Click + New Menu to create a new menu group by entering
   a Title and Slug.

M A N A G E M E N U

•  Click Manage to open the menu builder. This page displays all top-level menu items in a vertical list. Drag
   items using the handle icons to reorder them. Each item shows its sequence number, display name, URL path,
  and available sub-items count.

M E N U  I T E M A C T I O N S


• + Sub: Add a dropdown or submenu item under that menu.

•  Edit: Modify the menu item details.

•  Delete: Remove the item from the menu.

•  Expand arrow: Click to view and manage existing sub-items under that menu.

A D D M E N U  I T E M



• Click + Add Item to create a top-level menu
  entry. The form includes:
• Header Title: Custom display name for the
  menu (overrides the category name if set).
• Header URL: Custom URL path (for example,
  /latest, /shorts).
• Link Title / Link URL: Additional link text
  and destination if needed.
•  Category: Optionally link directly to an
  existing category.
• Open in new tab: Check to open the link in a
  new browser tab.

S U B M E N U  I T E M S

• When a menu item has sub-items, expanding it shows a nested list. In the example, the জাতীয় (National) menu contains
   three sub-items: কূটনীতি (Diplomacy), সংসদ (Parliament), and সরকার (Government).

• Add Sub Item

•  Click + Sub on any menu item to add a dropdown entry. Choose the Type:

•  Subcategory: Select an existing subcategory from the dropdown to link automatically.

•  Custom Link: Manually enter a Title and URL (for example, /tag/custom).

•  Check Open in new tab if needed, then click Save to add the sub-item.

G O L D  P R I C E M A N A G E M E N T

•  This page allows administrators to manage and update daily precious metal prices displayed on the website. It is
   divided into two sections: Gold & Silver Price (স  োনার দাম) and Copper Price (কপার দাম).

•  Gold & Silver Price

• The first table manages gold and silver rates by karat. Each row represents a different purity level (for example, 22
   karat, 21 karat, 18 karat, and traditional/sanaton gold). The columns include:

•  Karat: The gold purity classification.

•  Price per gram (৳): The base price per gram in BDT.

•  Price per bhari (৳): The price per bhari (a traditional South Asian unit), automatically calculated using the formula
  shown in the header (gram × 11.664).

•  Price per ana (৳): The price per ana, calculated as (gram × 0.729).

•  Price per rati (৳): The price per rati, calculated as (gram × 0.1215).

•  Last updated: Shows the user who last modified the row and the timestamp.

•  Copper Price

• The second table follows a similar structure for copper rates across different categories or purity levels. Each row
   has editable fields for the gram price and the calculated derivative prices.

• How to Update

•  Click into any price input field to edit the value. The system uses the gram price as the base and automatically
   calculates the other columns based on the displayed formulas. After making changes, scroll to the bottom and click
  Update to save the new prices. Click Cancel to discard changes. A notice at the top confirms that saving will update
   today's prices, and the Last updated timestamp refreshes accordingly.

•  This section manages sports tournament standings and point tables displayed on the website.

•  Tournament List

• The main page lists all created tournaments. Each row shows the tournament name, number of teams, activation
   status, last updated timestamp, and an edit button. Use the search bar to find tournaments by name. Click + Add
  Tournament to create a new point table.

•  Toggle the Status switch to Active to display the tournament on the website, or set it to Inactive to hide it.

• Add Point Table / Create Tournament

•  Click + Add Tournament to set up a new tournament standings table.

•  Tournament Name: Enter the tournament title (required), for example "Asia Cup 2026".

•  Active: Toggle on to make the point table visible on the public website.

•  Teams Section

• Add teams to the point table using the inline form:

•  Team: Enter the team name (required).

•  Play: Number of matches played.

•  Won: Matches won.

•  Loss: Matches lost.

•  Draw: Drawn matches.

• No Result: Matches with no result.

•  Net Run Rate: The team's net run rate.

•  Point: Total points earned.

•  Click + Add more to add additional team rows. Use the arrow buttons to reorder teams, or the delete button
   to remove a row.

•  Important Notes

•  You can type in Bangla or English. All values are saved exactly as entered.

•  Only the Team Name is required. Completely empty rows are ignored.

• The website displays teams in the exact order you set in this form.

•  Click Save to publish the point table, or Cancel to discard changes.

•  This analytics page provides a detailed report of published news stories and their view counts. The top summary
  badges show the total number of stories in the current report, total views, and how many stories have not yet
  been synced with the analytics system.

•  Filters & Search

•  Use the filter panel to narrow down the report results:

•  Published From / Published To: Select a date range to filter stories by their publication date in Bangladesh time.

•  Headline: Search for stories containing specific words in the headline.

•  Author: Filter by stories containing a specific author name.

•  News Slug: Search using the story's URL slug or ID.

•  Category: Filter by the assigned story category.

•  Story Type: Filter by content type (for example, News, Video story, Photo story).

•  Owner: Filter by the story owner or modifier.

•  Rows: Choose how many results to display per page (for example, 25 or 50).

•  Click Apply to execute the filtered search, or Reset to clear all filters and return to the full list.

•  Report Table

• The results table displays each story with the following columns:

•  Headline: The story title, with the story slug and ID shown underneath.

•  Type: The format of the content (for example, News).

•  Category: The assigned category and subcategory.

•  Author: The story's author.

•  Owner / Modifier: The user who owns or last modified the story.

•  Published: The exact publication date and time.

•  Views: The total number of views the story has received.

•  Synced: The synchronization status with the analytics system (for example, "pending").

•  Export

•  Click the Excel or CSV buttons at the top right to download the current report results in your preferred format.

•  Filtered Results

•  After applying filters, the summary badges and table update to show only the matching stories. In the example,
   filtering by date range, headline keyword, news slug, category (showbiz), story type (News), and owner (Md.
   Rabiullah) narrows the result down to a single matching story.

N E W S U S E R R E P O RT

•  This analytics page tracks and compares content creation and modification activity across all CMS users over a
   selected time period.

•  Quick Date Filters

•  At the top, one-click buttons let you instantly switch between preset reporting periods:

•  Today: Shows only today's activity.

•  Last 7 days: Shows the previous week of data.

•  Last 30 days: Shows the last 30 days of activity.

•  Last month: Shows the previous calendar month.

•  Last 3 months: Shows the last quarter of data.

•  Clicking any of these automatically updates the date range fields and refreshes the report.

• Summary Badges

•  Below the quick filters, colored badges display key metrics for the selected period:

•  Date range: The current reporting period (for example, "02 Nov 2026" or "04 Oct 2026 – 02 Nov 2026").

•  Users: Total number of active users in the selected range.

•  Created: Total stories created across all users.

•  Modified: Total stories modified across all users.

•  Views: Total views accumulated in the period.

•  Filter Panel

•  For more precise reporting, use the filter fields:

•  Report By: Select the grouping dimension (for example, "User").

•  From / To: Pick a custom date range using the date pickers.

•  User Name: Search for a specific user by typing their name.

•  Sort By: Choose how to order results (for example, "Created (most)" to rank by highest contributors first).

•  Rows: Set how many users to display per page (for example, 25 or 50).

•  Click Apply to generate the filtered report, or Reset to clear custom filters.

•  Report Table

•  The results table ranks users by their activity and performance:

•  User: The user's name and ID. Click the name to view detailed user activity.

•  Created: Number of stories the user created in the selected period.

•  Modified: Number of stories the user edited or updated. Some cells show "(X others)" indicating additional
   modifications on stories originally created by other users.

•  Total Views: Combined page views for all stories by that user.

•  Avg / Story: Average views per story for that user.

•  Pending Sync: Number of stories awaiting analytics synchronization.

• A Total row at the bottom sums up all columns across every user in the selected range.

•  Export

•  Click the Excel or CSV buttons at the top right to download the current report data in your preferred spreadsheet
   format.

•  Usage Example

•  In the screenshots, selecting Today shows 4 users with 12 created and 12 modified stories. Switching to Last 7 days
  expands to 8 users with 207 created and 213 modified stories. Selecting Last 30 days shows 10 users with 556
   created and 556 modified stories. Choosing Last month (October 2026) displays 10 users with 500 created and 499
  modified stories. Finally, Last 3 months shows the broadest range with 10 users, 556 created, and 556 modified
   stories.

A C T I V I T Y L O G

•  This page tracks every create, update, and delete action performed across the CMS. The top summary bar shows Total
   Actions, Created, Updated, Deleted, Unique Users, and Modules affected within the selected time range.

•  Quick Range & Filters

•  Use the quick range buttons (Today, Yesterday, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days) to instantly filter the log by time period. For
  more precise control, use the advanced filters:

•  From / To: Select a custom date and time range.

•  Module: Filter by the CMS module where the action occurred (for example, FeaturedNews, News, Category).

•  Action: Filter by action type (for example, BulkUpdate, Create, Update, Delete).

•  User: Filter by the specific user who performed the action.

•  Record or headline contains: Search by record name or news headline.

•  Record ID: Find actions on a specific record by its ID.

•  Sort: Order results by newest first or other criteria.

•  Per page: Control how many log entries display at once.

•  Click Apply Filters to execute the search, or Reset to clear all filters. Click Export CSV to download the current
   filtered results.

•  Log List Table

•  Each row represents one tracked action with the following details:

• When: Exact date and time of the action.

•  User: The user who performed the action, including their ID.

•  Module: The section of the CMS where the change happened.

•  Action: The type of action (for example, BulkUpdate).

•  Record: The specific item that was changed, with a brief description.

•  Changed: Number of fields that were modified (for example, "26 fields").

•  IP: The IP address from which the action was performed.

•  View: Click to open the full detail page for that specific log entry.

•  Activity Log Detail

•  Clicking View opens the detailed audit page for a single action (for example, "Log Entry #12059"). The header
  shows the action type, module, target record, user, timestamp, and a description of what was done.

•  Field Comparison

• The main section displays a table comparing Old Value and New Value for every field that changed. Each modified
  item is listed with an index number (for example, [0], [1]) and marked with a modified badge. This makes it easy to
   see exactly what data was replaced.

• Show Unchanged Fields

•  Toggle Show unchanged fields to expand the comparison and display fields that were part of the record but did not
  change during the edit. This is useful for reviewing the complete state of the data.

• Raw Stored Values

•  Click Raw stored values to expand a code view showing the full OldValues and NewValues in their raw structured format
   (similar to JSON). This displays the exact stored data objects with all properties such as newsId, position, and
  headline, allowing for deep technical inspection of the changes.

•  This section provides a comprehensive audit trail of all actions performed across the CMS. The top summary
   bar shows Total Actions, Successful actions, Failed actions, Validation Failed counts, Unique Users, and Unique

•  Quick Range & Filters

•  From / To: Custom date and time range.
•  Entity Type: Filter by the type of content (for example, news, category, tag).
•  Entity ID: Search for a specific record by its ID.
•  Action: Filter by action type (for example, create, update, lock_released, featured_position_changed).

•  Title contains: Search by article or record title.
•  Changed Field: Search for specific fields that were modified (for example, "Title").
•  IP Address: Filter by the IP address where the action originated.
•  Correlation ID: Search by a specific request UUID to track related actions.
•  Per page: Control how many entries display at once.
•  Click Apply Filters to execute the search, Reset to clear filters, or toggle Only failures to show unsuccessful
   actions only. Click Export CSV to download the filtered results.

•  Audit List Table

•  Each row represents one tracked action with the following details:

•  When: Exact date and time of the action.

•  User: The user who performed the action.

•  Action: The type of action (for example, lock_released, update, featured_position_changed), displayed as a colored badge.

•  Entity: The content type and ID affected (for example, news #569).

•   Title: The headline or name of the affected record.

•  Status: Whether the action succeeded or failed.

•  Changed: Number of fields modified (for example, "5 fields").

•  Duration: How long the action took to process.

•  IP: The IP address from which the action was performed.

•  View: Opens the detailed audit page for that specific action.

•  Timeline: Opens the full chronological timeline for the affected entity.

•  Audit Detail Page

•  Clicking View opens the full audit detail for a single action (for example, "Audit Detail #1869"). The header shows:

•  The action type and status (for example, lock_released, Success).

•  The affected entity (for example, news #569) and its title.

•  The user who performed the action, timestamp, and IP address.

•  Field Changes

•  For actions that modified data, a Field Changes table compares Old Value and New Value for every changed field. In the
   example, an update action shows changes to Last Published At, Locked, Locked At, Locked By, and Pinned
  in categories. Switch between Plain Text, Rich Preview, and Raw view modes at the top right of the changes table.

•  Related Events

•  The detail page also shows Related Events, listing other actions that occurred in the same request. Each related event
   displays its time, action type, status, and a link to view its own detail page. The Correlation ID at the bottom links all
   actions from the same request together.

•  Full Timeline

•  Clicking Timeline on any audit row opens the Full Timeline for that specific entity (for example, news #569). This view
  shows every event ever recorded for that item in chronological order, grouped by date. Each event displays:

•  The action type badge (for example, create, update, featured_position_changed, lock_released).

•  The user who performed it and their IP address.

•  The exact timestamp.

•  All fields that were changed, shown as inline tags.

•  View Diff and All from request buttons for deeper inspection.

•  The timeline summary bar at the top shows Total Events, Successful, Failed, and Unique Users for that entity's history.
   Click Back to Report to return to the main audit list.
